newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH UNIONS, EMPLOYERS AGREE EMU RESOLUTION.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH UNIONS, EMPLOYERS AGREE EMU RESOLUTION.

text.p: Finland's leading trade union groups and biggest employer confederations on Thursday signed a joint resolution saying workers' nominal wages would not have to be cut if Finland joined European economic and monetary union.

The labour market organisations reaffirmed their commitment to low inflation, saying their traget remained that the rise in prices in Finland should not exceed the average rise in prices in European Union countries.
They further said it was important that the European Central Bank's inflation target should be such that it does not lead to deflation.

"The central labour market organisations state that the targets for economic policy should be to promote economic growth, improve employment, maintain competitiveness, and low inflation and keeping public debt under control," the resolution said, adding these targets were valid both in and outside EMU.
Referring to the implementation of the EMU budget stability pact, the organisations said it should be possible to take Finland's "special conditions" into account, but did not elaborate.
Finland's tripartite collective bargaining system would become even more important in the new circumstances, they said.
"The central labour market organisations state that EMU-membership does not involve touching minimum terms of agreements or their general coverage, or cuts in nominal wages," the resolution said.
The organisations said they would work towards maintaining various options for the structure of future pay deals, including centralised nation-wide agreements.

"Adjusting permanently to conditions of low inflation is a central EMU-related challenge for (pay) agreement activities Current bargaining systems make it possible to keep wage development in line with the inflation target," they said.

The organisations also agreed to start work on so called buffer arrangements to cushion the impact of economic disturbances. They agreed to work on this issue in such a way that conditions for decisions on cyclical buffer arrangements would be in place this autumn, the resolution said.
